govdocs-archive_org-nsia-IconoclastDalla: This letter to the Dallas Iconoclast — June 2, 1975, creator unknown — is a press note. The Iconoclast was an alternative weekly. Letters shaped the paper. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.

proserpine-and-midas: Mary Shelley — author of Frankenstein — wrote these two short verse plays on Greek myths in 1820. Proserpine tells of the goddess carried off to the underworld; Midas dramatizes the king whose golden touch became a curse. Published long after her death, they reveal Shelley's classical learning and her gift for giving old myths fresh feeling.
the-cruise-of-the-kawa-wanderings-in-the: Behind the pen name Walter E. Traprock, humorist George Chappell sails the South Seas in this delicious parody of travel writing. The Kawa's voyage through tropical islands mocks every cliché of the intrepid-explorer book with a straight face. Readers who enjoy a good literary joke will find it as funny now as when it first appeared.
the-belted-seas: Arthur Colton's novel takes readers to tropical seas and distant islands, where adventure and romance unfold under southern skies. His tales of the Pacific carry the salt air of firsthand knowledge. An engaging period novel for lovers of faraway places.
the-orations-of-lysias: Lysias — the great Athenian speechwriter — pleads cases of murder, treason, and civic duty in these masterful orations. His plain, powerful style made him the model of Attic prose for all antiquity. Ancient rhetoric at its most human and dramatic. Law students and lovers of Athens alike still thrill to his direct, devastating eloquence.
the-countess-of-escarbagnas: Molière's Countess of Escarbagnas — the provincial lady aping Parisian airs and graces — provides broad, merry comedy. His satire of social climbing and small-town pretension never misses its mark. A merry minor Molière, full of laughs. Paris laughs at her; the provinces recognize themselves.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abdias: This 1913 reference article on Abdias — Obadiah the prophet, whose short book threatens Edom. Francis Gigot weighs its date and meaning. The smallest Old Testament book gets full treatment. A solid guide to a brief prophecy. Edom's pride falls in his twenty-one verses.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-achimaas: A 1913 entry on Achimaas — Zadok's son, the swift runner of David's wars. Wendell Reilly tells his fleet-footed tale. He outran the Cushite with good news. The Bible's fleetest messenger. David trusted him with secret messages. His speed saved the kingdom twice.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-acuas: A 1913 entry on Acuas — a name in the early Manichaean story. John Joseph A'Becket notes the scanty record. The sect's eastern roots show here. A footnote to the history of heresy. Mani's shadow falls across the entry. The heresy spread from Persia west.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-addas: This 1913 reference piece on Addas — a name in the Manichaean mission story. Thomas Walsh records the thin tradition. The heresy spread through such wanderers. A shadowy figure of the third century. Little more is known. Augustine refuted the sect he briefly joined.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adonias: A 1913 entry on Adonias — Adonijah, David's handsome son who grasped at the crown. Francis Gigot tells his brief revolt. Solomon's justice ended his hopes. Ambition's price, paid at the altar. A prince who reached too high. His mother Haggith wept for her lost son.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-agathias: A 1913 entry on Agathias — the Byzantine poet and historian. Thomas Shahan notes his histories and epigrams. He sang in Justinian's learned court. His verses grace the Greek Anthology. A lawyer with a poet's soul. His Daphniaca sang of love and wine.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alagoas: This 1913 reference piece on Alagoas — the Brazilian diocese of the northeast. John Joseph A'Becket gives its story. Sugar plantations framed its parishes. The faith grew with the colony. A tropical see of old Brazil. Its bishop faces the Atlantic surf.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ampurias: This 1913 reference article on Ampurias — Empúries, the old Greek city of Spain. John Joseph A'Becket notes its Christian past. Its bishops sat in the Visigothic councils. Ruins guard the Catalan shore. A see of ancient Iberia. Its mosaics grace the Barcelona museum.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: This 1913 reference article on the ancient see of Strängnäs — the Swedish lake bishopric. Arthur Taylor tells its story. Its bishops served the Mälar towns. The Vasas seized its lands. A vanished see of Sweden. Its tower watches the lake waters.

This 1913 reference piece on the ancient see of Västerås — the Swedish lake bishopric. Arthur Taylor gives its story. Its bishops watched the iron districts. Gustavus seized its wealthy lands. A vanished see of the Swedes. Its castle guarded the lake strait.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andres-perez-: This 1913 reference article on Andrés Pérez de Ribas — the Jesuit historian of the northwest missions. James Mooney praises his Historia. His pages lit Sinaloa and Sonora. The missions' classic chronicler. A soldier's pen in a priest's hand. His Triumphs celebrated the mission martyrs.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-annas: A 1913 entry on Annas — the high priest of the Passion. Edward Arbez tells his dark part. Christ stood bound before his court. His house ruled the temple politics. The power behind the priesthood. His palace saw the night trial. His kin filled the high priesthood.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-de-he: This 1913 reference article on Antonio de Herrera — the chronicler of the Indies. Camillus Crivelli honors his Décadas. His pages told the conquest's tale. Philip's court prized his pen. The historian of the New World. His Descripción mapped the Indies' coasts.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aristeas: A 1913 entry on Aristeas — the Letter of Aristeas and the Septuagint's legend. The entry tells the famous tale. Seventy translators made the Greek Bible. The scholars sift fact from fable. The legend of the translated law. His letter charmed the ancient readers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arkansas: A 1913 entry on Arkansas — the young diocese of Little Rock. Charles Sloane tells its pioneer tale. The frontier tested its first bishops. The Ozarks guard its quiet towns. A bishopric of the new South. Its cathedral crowns the river bluff.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-armella-nicol: A 1913 entry on Armella Nicolas — a mystic of the Breton countryside. Edward Garesché honors her holy life. The entry preserves her modest fame. The poor maid's visions edified many. A saint of the humble folk. Her tomb draws the Breton pilgrims.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arras: This 1913 reference article on Arras — the French diocese of Artois. Georges Goyau gives its story. Its cathedral crowns the market town. The Great War scarred its stones. A see of the northern plain. Its belfry crowns the market square. Its tapestries were Europe's finest.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-association-o: This 1913 reference piece on the association of ideas — the psychology of linked thoughts. Edmund Wirth treats it scholastically. The mind binds its memories. The schools refined the doctrine. The philosophy of memory's chain. Its laws explain the wandering mind. Its study aids the confessors' art.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-athenagoras: This 1913 reference piece on Athenagoras — the Christian thinker of Athens — honors his plea. John Bertram Peterson wrote it up. His Embassy spoke to the emperors. He begged fair play for the Church. A sage with a Christian heart. His book survives whole to this day.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-auguste-nicol: A 1913 entry on Auguste Nicolas — the apologist of the Études philosophiques. Antoine Dégert honors his zealous pen. His volumes defended the faith. The magistrate became the Church's champion. A layman among the defenders. His Art of Believing convinced thousands.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-banaias: A 1913 entry on Banaias — Banias, Caesarea Philippi, now a titular see. John Tierney notes its scriptural fame. Peter confessed Christ by its springs. The Church keeps its ancient name. A see of the Holy Land. Its springs feed the Jordan's source.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartolomeu-di: A 1913 entry on Bartolomeu Dias — the rounder of the Cape of Storms. Otto Hartig honors his daring voyage. His caravels passed the southern cape. The sea road to India opened. Portugal's pioneer of the oceans. His padrão still marks the cape.
